findings.read_only_database_catalog_and_aggregate: Production lacks the two durable tables. Staging has both tables in the default schema and no active durable leases at the time of review. The production pending inventory includes historical start markers and no immediately eligible zero-attempt rows under the conservative review predicate.
findings.local_postgresql_16_rehearsal: Initialized a synthetic database with the exact production image. Candidate startup added only the two durable tables, preserved a synthetic legacy row, and was rerunnable. The old image started with the tables retained. A synthetic pre-change dump restored to a separate database with the same row digest. Provider execution remained disabled and the durable tables stayed empty.
findings.backup_metadata: Automated backups and point-in-time recovery are configured and recent backup runs succeeded. Managed restore duration and the recovery point for the actual change window remain unverified.
findings.read_only_runtime_inventory: The release images enforce freeze on API, worker and confirmed administrative commands. The production deployment region has no production-bound candidate worker, dedicated queue or scheduler. The current legacy revision serves all traffic and cannot observe the candidate gate. Existing production API and administrative job point to the same production database configuration, distinct from staging.

gates.requires: Record a fresh recovery point, verified migration lock bounds and a single migration executor at the eventual approved change window. The synthetic timing is planning evidence; no production restore was run.

Maintain the existing service URL, verify every live route goes to a frozen revision, remove legacy tags, hold manual launches, and reconcile image, progressive text and provider activity against the fence boundary. A bare route rollback to old code reopens generation.
Keep the preflight-only worker and read-only role, empty paused queue, paused scheduler and production provider execution disabled until approved activation.

Keep candidate frozen and delivery paused if legacy remains reachable, in-flight outcomes are unknown, or any identity, database or delivery check fails. Restore old traffic only with verified independent fencing or a separately approved decision. Preserve tables, markers and provider evidence.
Execute only the approved frozen cutover in its confirmed window. Keep production dispatch paused and paid image and text generation held.

rollback_summary: Freeze new provider work. Pause dispatch and delivery. Observe in-flight execution, leases and unresolved provider reservations.
Return traffic to the captured rollback revision only after fencing old and new generation paths. Keep additive tables and the provider ledger.
Keep generation paused during reconciliation. If schema or data recovery is required, verify a separate restore before any recovery traffic decision.

failures: First fixture setup stopped before mutation when the staging database URL used a different driver syntax from the URL parser. Setup resumed after using the application database URL parser.
An initial Secret Manager grant was rejected while the new fixture service account propagated. The scoped grants and fixture deployment were later verified.

The first setup attempt used the wrong REST separator for the Scheduler resume action. The job never resumed or triggered in that attempt and its target was restored. The action path was corrected before the one authorized trigger.

The deleted temporary service account returned an ambiguous denial on direct lookup. Cleanup verification switched to the project account inventory.
unverified: The caller had the direct invoker grant when inspected afterward. The request-time effective IAM decision and cause of the observed rejection remain unverified. The operator lacked caller impersonation and access to the effective IAM troubleshooter.

diagnostic.isolated_root_cause: The isolated Scheduler used the exact short job name in its request header. The original substitute accepted only the project-ID and project-number full resource forms. Signed token, audience, expected email and subject, and the legacy boolean email verification check all passed.

failures: The original fixture reproduced an application HTTP 403 after correctly authenticating the isolated Scheduler. The job-name check alone failed.
unverified: The production rerun is held. Historical production logs did not capture the header shape; the isolated test reproduces the failure with the same original matcher and a real Cloud Scheduler. No production action is implied.
